votes.refutation: I first checked whether all queued IDs were attacker-supplied as the claim implies. They are actually derived by the receiver from the real task/team/reviewer, so arbitrary Celery arguments alone are not the exploit. The URL remains independently writable, however, and a real task plus an unrelated URL passes all the source-side guards. The normal webhook's bot/native/task checks (stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:169-205) are not reused here. The marker enables the bot/draft exception (temporal/activities.py:448-451; review_local.py:321-326), and publication only checks head/supersession before approval (activities.py:673-745). The unbound PR target, rather than arbitrary provenance IDs by themselves, proves the defect.
